Is food one of your best memories or highlight of travel?  I know we are always looking for great local food, but when you can take a cooking class from the famous Paula Deen, that’s even better.  This was several years ago, but I came away with great memories and recipes.   Crab Cakes – one of our favorite foods, at home, or maybe try at a restaurant.  This Savannah Crab Cake recipe is a winner in my family, and sure it will be for your families’s as well.

I can be picky about things like Crab Cakes or Alfredo Sauce at restaurants since I LOVE my recipes for these so much.  My husband isn’t a real seafood lover, but this is something he will eat.  You can find my  Alfredo Sauces below.

Savannah Crab Cake Cooking Class with Paula Deen

In the summer of 2004, we had a great vacation in Savannah and Tybee Island.  But one of the highlights for me was attending a cooking class with Paula Deen.  She had just married Michael and was still in the beginning stages of her empire. 

When I saw a class being held the week I was visiting, I had to go.  Plus, to my delight it was about seafood.  Even then it wasn’t cheap, but I knew it was probably a once in a lifetime chance.  It was held in the basement of The Lady & Sons Restaurant in downtown Savannah and was a small, intimate group.  What you saw on TV is what she was in person, along with Jamie, Michael, and Aunt Peggy.  There was time for speaking to all of these, autographs and photos.

The restaurant closed recently taking away one of the more popular restaurants when visiting the Savanah or Tybee Island area.  We ate there a couple times and always enjoyed it and thought the food was good.

 

This class and recipe even got me a feature in our  local newspaper.

 

Savannah Crab Cake Recipe

Crab Cake Mixture
  • 3 T butter
  • 3 green onions, finely chopped
  • ½ C finely chopped bell pepper
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 4 ½ t heavy cream
  • ¼ C mayonnaise
  • ½ C panko crumbs
  • 1 egg
  • 2 T fresh parsley, chopped
  • 1 lb fresh crabmeat (if any juice – drain)
  • Juice of ½ lemon

Coating Mixture

Approximately 3/4 cup each

  • Parmesan cheese
  • Panko crumbs
  • 3 T butter
  • 3 T olive oil

Melt butter in skillet – saute’ onion, garlic and green pepper until peppers are limp.  Do not brown.  Place in mixing bowl and cool.  Add cream and mustard and mix well.  Add cracker crumbs, egg, parsley, mayonnaise and lemon juice.  Mix well.  Gently fold in crab meat, being careful to not crush it.  Form into patties.

Mix together Parmesan cheese and cracker crumbs.  Gently coat each patty in this mixture.  Refrigerate about 2 hours to firm up or until you are ready to use.

Fry on medium heat in the butter and olive oil about 3 minutes per side.

NOTES:

If the mixture is a bit too thin to form patties, add a few more crumbs but be careful not to add too many since you want the taste of crab and not panko filling

Using a mixture of butter and olive oil gives it a bit more flavor plus the olive oil helps prevent the butter from browning and burning too easily

These can also be made into small balls to use as appetizers, 1” – 1 ½”

Depending on the wetness of your patty, you might need a bit more cheese and cracker crumbs for coating.  You don’t really want the coating too heavy

Shore is Good Seafood Dip

Another recipe which came out of this class was this Seafood Dip – another family favorite even for my non-seafood loving husband.  This is made with a lot of shrimp and crab.

Savannah Crab Cakes by Paula Deen

No Ratings

This is a version of a crab cake I got the recipe from during a Paula Deen Cooking Class several years ago. It's very close to her own, but I made it my own. Hope you enjoy all the great crab flavor.

Ingredients

  • Crab Cakes
  • 3 T butter
  • 3 green onions, finely chopped
  • ½ C finely chopped bell pepper
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 4 ½ t heavy cream
  • ¼ C mayonnaise
  • ½ C panko crumbs
  • 1 egg
  • 2 T fresh parsley, chopped
  • 1 lb fresh crabmeat (if any juice - drain)
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • Coating
  • Approximately 3/4 cup each
  • Parmesan cheese
  • Panko crumbs
  • 3 T butter
  • 3 T olive oil

Instructions

  1. Crab Cakes

    2. Melt butter in skillet

    Add onions, garlic and green pepper and saute’ until peppers are limp, but not brown

    Place this mixture in medium mixing bowl to cool

    After cool, add cream and mustard, mix well

    Add panko crumbs, egg, parsley, mayonnaise, and lemon juice, mix well

    Gently fold in crab meat, being careful not to crush the crab meat.

    Form into 2” patties

    Coating

    Mix Parmesan cheese and panko crumbs in bowl

    Coat each patty in this mixture

    Refrigerate for about 2 hours, or freeze about 30 minutes until ready to cook

    Fry on medium heat in the butter and olive oil mixture

    Cook approximately 3 minutes per side

    Drain on rack or paper towels


    Refrigerate any leftovers up to 3 days

Notes

If the mixture is a bit too thin to form patties, add a few more crumbs but be careful not to add too many since you want the taste of crab and not panko filling


Using a mixture of butter and olive oil gives it a bit more flavor plus the olive oil helps prevent the butter from browning and burning too easily


These can also be made into small balls to use as appetizers, 1” – 1 ½”


Depending on the wetness of your patty, you might need a bit more cheese and cracker crumbs for coating.  You don't really want the coating too heavy
